subject: Science
stem: A plane mirror always forms an image that is virtual, erect and of the same size as the object, but with one distinguishing feature. That feature is:

options.option_text: Lateral inversion — left and right appear interchanged
The image is always smaller than the object
The image is always inverted (upside down)
The image can be caught on a screen

explanation: Plane mirrors laterally invert images (why 'AMBULANCE' is written mirror-reversed on ambulance fronts) but keep the same size and orientation (erect), and the image is virtual — it cannot be caught on a screen.

section: Science · Ch43 — Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: We feel the warmth of a bonfire even while standing a few metres away, without any air current reaching us. This heat reaches us mainly by:

options.option_text: Radiation
Conduction
Convection
Evaporation

explanation: Radiation transfers heat via electromagnetic waves through air (or vacuum) without needing a medium or particle movement. Conduction needs direct contact; convection needs fluid/air current movement.

section: Science · Ch43 — Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum (such as outer space) because sound is a:

options.option_text: Mechanical wave requiring a material medium to propagate
Form of electromagnetic radiation like light
Chemical reaction between air molecules
Type of magnetic field disturbance

explanation: Sound travels by vibrating particles of a medium (solid, liquid, or gas); with no particles in a vacuum, sound cannot propagate. Light, unlike sound, is electromagnetic and needs no medium.

subject: Science
stem: In a string of old-style decorative bulbs wired in series, if one bulb fuses, all the other bulbs go off. This happens because a series circuit:

options.option_text: Provides only a single path for current, which is broken when any one component fails
Provides multiple paths, so failure of one bulb should not matter
Increases voltage across the remaining bulbs to keep them glowing
Automatically bypasses the broken bulb

explanation: A series circuit has only one current path; a break anywhere (a fused filament) stops current everywhere in the loop. A parallel circuit, in contrast, would let other bulbs keep glowing if one fails.

section: Science · Ch43 — Light, Heat, Sound, Electricity & Magnetism
subject: Science
stem: When a bar magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece becomes:

options.option_text: A complete new magnet with its own north and south poles
A single isolated north pole and a single isolated south pole
Non-magnetic, since breaking destroys magnetism
Only a north pole in both pieces

explanation: Magnetic poles always occur in pairs; breaking a magnet never isolates a single pole — each fragment becomes a smaller complete magnet with both a north and a south pole (monopoles do not exist in ordinary magnets).
